precepts.text: Uzziel and Hananiah repaired their sections, and next to them Rephaiah, ruler of the half part of Jerusalem, a supervisor over an area. Offices have leads entrusted with more. If you are overwhelmed for the Lord, that is a beautiful stress; ask for more laborers and pray and fast for them rather than complain, because the Lord put you in that office.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

precepts.why:
This is the rebuilding of Jerusalem. “Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.” Each man repaired his own section of the wall. Then: “And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.” The ruler of the half part: he was a supervisor over that area.

That is leadership. When you come in the truth you may just edit the video, go on the fly mission, or work in the kitchen. At some point you become over the office: now you are over the brothers that are editing, over the IT team, over the building team, over the sisters. Now your job changes, because you have people under you. Everybody is not built for that level. You are not in charge; you are responsible for those in your charge. In IUIC there are different offices with leads in place, and a man who was once responsible for one office, the Lord entrusted him with more.

Sometimes brothers get overwhelmed, and that will happen. But there is no better thing than to be overwhelmed for the Lord. You do not have a demon on your back, you are not behind bars, you are not suffering illness; you are stressed out for the Lord's work, and that is a beautiful thing. So do not complain. Come up and say, I need more assistance in this office. Pray and fast for more laborers, and rejoice in it, because the Lord gave you that office and put you in that position.

points: The high priest and his brethren the priests begin the work by building the sheep gate, sanctifying it, and setting up its doors as far as the tower of Meah and the tower of Hananeel.
The rebuilding starts with the priests, showing that the sanctified work of the Most High is set in order first before the rest of the wall is raised.

note.label: Nehemiah 3: The Builders of the Wall

points: The sons of Hassenaah build the fish gate, laying its beams and setting up its doors, locks, and bars.
Each gate is named and each family assigned, so the record shows a people organized and accountable for their portion of the work.

note.label: Nehemiah 3: The Builders of the Wall

points: The Tekoites repair their section, but their nobles will not put their necks to the work of their Lord.
Not everyone among the people is willing to labor. The nobles who hold back are marked out, showing that the work of the Most High separates those who serve from those who spare themselves.

note.label: Nehemiah 3: The Builders of the Wall

points: Shallum the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem repairs his portion, he and his daughters.
The daughters are named as builders alongside the men, showing the whole household given to the work.

note.label: Nehemiah 3: The Builders of the Wall

points: Between the going up of the corner and the sheep gate the goldsmiths and the merchants make their repairs.
The chapter closes the circuit of the wall with a long roll of the houses and trades that each took a piece, every man over against his own house.
